newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Inchcape clears decks for expansion.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Inchcape clears decks for expansion.

text.p: Inchcape Plc announced a 12 percent rise in headline profits on Monday and said it would now be investing for expansion, to fill the gap left by last year's clear-out of non-core businesses.
The multinational car dealer to soft drinks bottler reported a pretax profit of 165.1 million pounds ($264.7 million) before exceptional items, compared with 146.8 million pounds in 1995.
Operating profits of 195 million pounds against 119.9 million pounds, on marginally lower sales of 6.26 billion pounds and the total dividend was raised five percent to 10.5 pence a share.

Group pretax profits jumped to 107 million pounds from 17.4 million pounds in 1995 but results were distorted by the sale of its Bain Hogg insurance and Testing Services businesses for a total of 540 million pounds.

Chairman Sir Colin Marshall said trading in the remaining businesses was expected to improve this year, although first-half results would show a big gap left by the sale of Bain Hogg, which now had to be filled.
"But we have got the company into a good position," he told Reuters. "We are confident of improvement from our continuing businesses."
The sale of Bain Hogg and Testing Services helped wipe out debts of nearly 500 million pounds to leave the group with net cash of 39.9 million pounds at the end of 1996.

"We have a strong balance sheet," Marshall said. "We are going to take our position cautiously as we go forward but we will look at opportunities for expanding what we already have and adding to it," he said.
The company wants to expand its car dealing businesses as well as develop its soft drinks operations, he said.
Last year operating profits at the Motors division increased 29 percent to 126.6 million pounds, helped by a strong performance from its Toyota franchises.

The company said the product marketing services business, which operates mainly in far and middle east, remained "disappointing", with profits falling seven percent to 30.2 million pounds but said restructuring was underway.
Singapore-listed affiliate Inchcape Berhad announced on Monday it was to demerge its marketing services operation to give current shareholders pro-rata shares in the new company.

Meanwhile operating profits in the soft drinks bottling business which has concentrated on developing new overseas markets for Coca-Cola Co, fell to 8.2 million pounds from 13 million despite sales doubling to 197.8 million pounds.
Inchcape said strong profits in Chile "were offset by substantial start-up losses in Russia as expected and by weakness in the Peruvian soft drinks market."
Inchcape announced on Monday that its Peruvian unit Embotelladora Latinoamericana SA (ELSA) had added to its repertoire by buying the San Luis table water and Kola Inglesa brands.
It also plans to open its third and fourth Coca-Cola bottling plants in Russia later this year.
